metadata.philosophy: Curator, not prescriber. Every element is available for any business. Choose by vibe and what feels right, not by industry rules.

sources.user_notes: Car speeding in the background like a video, beautiful product dash, the scroll cursor being represented with a red circle, overall beauty of the color palette

Fade in effect of the big banner in the home page and the we've partnered with hover of logos, also the proven process section is a really nice layout, AND THE team section rotating image bar. Also the services section of all the cards fading in and out with a 3d effect.

The 3d dot animation in the back of the home page, large and interesting text. The sentence writes itself as you scroll down with the 3d blocks to the right. The way our work fades in with modular feel. The smart analytics charts flowing together. Pricing model and our work also beautiful.

The mockups of the product are exceptional and the color gradients are neat, love the way the boxes come together and the visuals in each box, as well as the dynamic diagrams, plus the beauty of the pricing model

Love the way text is being typed as you move through the website, the buyers moving down the screen dynamically in the voice assistants, the tool integrations flowing in beautifully, and the our results numbers going up live, love the rotating client testimonial cards too, the why choose us check list and the interestingness of the text, and the nice format of our team

Love the big text of the business in white blocks that come up, the background video of the two guys that comes up in super clear resolution as you scroll (this is beautiful), elegant project blocks, and nice black minimalistic colors

I love the text on the front of the landing page and the text sliding in the bar. The rotating questions in removing the roadblocks is really cool - one row left one right. Elegant icons, numbers section, services cards slide down in animation where you're not moving down the page. Process part rotating around the globe as you scroll, with us vs without us table, artistic testimonials, redesigned FAQ section, big logo at bottom

3D element of the dashboard moves towards you on the screen as you scroll down, beautiful backgrounds with cloud and sky, love the way image zooms out as you scroll for mobile app and web app, love the way customer reviews move horizontally, and the way everything fades in, love the project management visual and the light color gradients

Love the way the big orange text of Arpeggio pans in right when you open with the bold blue background of the woman, and the background card that feels like a movie theater preview. Rectangular components like Boreal pan out on the side as you scroll, sections cover each other as you scroll. Numbers calculate in real time with pac man. What we do pans in to fill whole screen. Why choose us with visuals numbers and rectangular cards spectacularly beautiful. Inspiring client experiences sliding testimonials. Bottom part becomes large and takes over the website.
I love the consistent color layout, the simple layout of the whole web page, the very clear process. This is one of the most simple ones by far and applies greatly to our SMB segment

Love the large background image of the vacuum, small amount of words but big text, get a free quote box makes it very simple. Spaces we specialize section with icons and stock images, the flow of how it works 1 2 3 4 with nice image cards. Why it works with different cards and numbers and colors

Love the very simple layout, the way everything pans in, reviews incorporation, subtle dots, offer a wide range of services, less text and nice rectangular sections with simple beautiful colors, our work process is great layout

I love the way images are utilized from the background image in the hero to book a call right away, meet the team, color palette, our services cards, green boxes, image gallery aesthetic layout with recent works, sliding trusted by customers with green sexy boxes

Love the beautiful image cards throughout — main section and gallery across screen, color palette, meet your instructor cards, simple class type rectangles with images, class schedule layout, about us location map was really nice

Like the choice of simplicity and fonts and the mission statement, meet your therapist section — tags and font of name under image plus the way rectangular sections cover each other up and move when you scroll down
Love the image cards and the way they drag across the screen, dotted background, italic words in the title. Sliding cards with images animating in opposite directions. Sliding reviews.

Exceptional video background, glassy feel, transparent testimonial boxes. Image cards become videos — really levels up a website. Small boxes throughout that elevate. Schedule and class catalogue is neat.
Love video in background, images sliding in different directions when you scroll. Sections take over the screen when you scroll down more.

STANDOUT for brands. Skin cream icon moves around the website as you scroll — exceptional. Sentence writes itself. Five reasons scroll away into new reason with each scroll. Step-by-step process with image fadeaway. Despite stock, images are very well chosen. 'What they are saying' in big text with flowing review cards.

STANDOUT for design. Chair in the middle is very well rendered. Rotating images on scroll. Featured product rotates as you scroll. Art material section with tree icons excellent. View preview icon click-through is really nice. Studio tour with playable content and rotating words. Collection and catalog elegantly presented with super high resolution images.

Beautiful renderings of sushi and ramen — extremely clever. Food rendered in a way that appetizes. Big text flows across screen nicely. Menu in huge appealing text divided into two segments. Chef picture with quote is a very nice design element.

Big impactful image overlay on front page. Containers broken out nicely with small business icons. Images in cards work well. Color palette is really clever and super simple. Testimonials flow together seamlessly. About us section incorporates story effectively.

STANDOUT — one of the best ever seen. Buy sell rent text is huge with blurred bg that becomes clearer on scroll. Listings have beautiful image cards with panning images. Neighborhood grid with moving images. Agency comparison with big bg image and checklist. Submit property form is exceptionally beautiful. Explore area fills half screen — clicking Brickell reveals a sexy flyer.

Opening yacht video is really good — super high resolution. Boats rendered beautifully. Reviews and video overlay of boats flowing through is nice. Yacht catalog cards extremely appealing. Error section has exceptional ocean video background. Want to find stock videos that replicate this quality.

STANDOUT for therapeutic. Big image fills whole screen — super powerful. About section with cards that zoom in starting transparent and below screen. Deep nature imagery with beautiful tree photos. Pricing with leaf sprouting over forest for most popular option is really creative.
Nailed the big hero images and product catalogs. Bold elegant design lets the cars shine through. Simple, effective.

Stands out for interactive animations. Hero flows beautifully — image cards animate in, text forms sentences, product videos sync with moving words. Founders section and partnership logos animate through screen with precision. Cards flow vertically. Studio team section ties everything together. One of the best designed — clever, fluid, intentional.
Simple, matching kid-oriented product. Camp counselors look friendly. Images flow well. Gallery collage is great. Event details are clear. Small design elements like triangles and circles stand out.

STANDOUT — most exceptional ever seen. Background speed-up of construction in faint sunlight is simply amazing. Scrolling about section with sentences appearing and images waving out. Moving metrics and numbers. Property catalogs visually stunning. Orient Sky Penthouse detail page with big image and components. Video plays then words hook you in. Blog grid with consistent panning images. Landowners section with property build animation is stunning. Even the contact form is cool.

font_pairings.notes: The workhorse pairing. Figtree's rounded terminals feel welcoming without sacrificing professionalism. Great for any business that wants to feel approachable.

font_pairings.next_font_import:
import { Inter } from 'next/font/google'
// Geist via next/font/local or @vercel/font
font_pairings.notes: Vercel's own font. Full weight range gives incredible flexibility. Feels cutting-edge and clean.

font_pairings.next_font_import:
// Satoshi via next/font/local (fontshare.com)
import { Inter } from 'next/font/google'
font_pairings.notes: Clean geometric sans with a calming quality. Works wonderfully when you want the site to feel serene and trustworthy.
The classic serif + sans combo. Playfair's high contrast strokes feel luxurious. Variable version supports optical sizing.

font_pairings.next_font_import:
import { Red_Hat_Mono, Inter } from 'next/font/google'
// Carattere via next/font/google
font_pairings.notes: Unusual triple-font system. Decorative script for impact, monospace for data/labels, Inter for body. Creates a layered, sophisticated typographic hierarchy.
Vietnamese-optimized but works beautifully for Latin text too. Slightly narrower and more compact than Inter — makes bold headlines pop.

font_pairings.next_font_import:
// Open Runde via next/font/local
import { Inter } from 'next/font/google'
font_pairings.notes: Even rounder than Figtree. Every corner is softened. Creates an incredibly welcoming, non-intimidating feel.

font_pairings.next_font_import:
// Switzer via next/font/local (fontshare.com)
import { Fragment_Mono, Inter } from 'next/font/google'
font_pairings.notes: Switzer is a clean geometric sans with slightly sharper geometry than Inter. Paired with Fragment Mono for technical labels/metadata.
Warm editorial serif that feels personal and inviting. Single weight but high impact at display sizes.
Geometric sans with distinctive character shapes. Feels more structured and technical than Figtree — confident without being cold.
Syne has unusual letter shapes that demand attention. Paired with the softer DM Sans for readability. For businesses with personality.
Classic transitional serif meets humanist sans. Communicates establishment and reliability.

font_pairings.next_font_import:
// Neue Haas Grotesk via next/font/local
import { Fragment_Mono, Inter } from 'next/font/google'
font_pairings.notes: The original Helvetica, in display form. Paired with monospace accents for a designer-portfolio feel.
Full monospace site. Every element in mono creates a systematized, data-driven aesthetic. Bold choice.
Ranchers is a chunky display font with personality. Caveat adds a handwritten touch. For businesses that don't take themselves too seriously.
Triple geometric sans stack. Outfit for large headlines, Poppins for section titles, Inter for body. Subtle hierarchy through similar but distinct fonts.
Extremely wide weight range (200-800) means one font can do whisper-thin labels AND bold headlines. Maximum flexibility.
Condensed fonts pack more text into headlines. Creates an information-dense, newspaper-like feel at large sizes.

font_pairings.next_font_import:
// Squeak Bold via next/font/local
// System sans for body
font_pairings.notes: PostHog's custom brand font. Shows that a single distinctive display font paired with system sans can create a strong brand identity cheaply.
Slightly rounder and softer than Inter at display sizes. Gentle, non-aggressive. Wonderful when you want warmth.

A refined serif with contemporary proportions. Reads as professional consulting without feeling stuffy. Pairs beautifully with Inter's neutrality. Great for any business that wants authority with approachability.

A variable grotesque with unusual letterform details — slightly quirky terminals and stroke endings that give it personality. Wide weight range. Feels like someone hand-picked each letter. For businesses that want to stand out with warmth.

Ultra-high contrast serif — thin hairlines and thick strokes create incredible drama at display sizes. Feels more luxurious than Playfair Display. Perfect for hospitality, design studios, premium services. The italic is especially beautiful.

font_pairings.next_font_import:
// General Sans via next/font/local (fontshare.com)
import { Inter } from 'next/font/google'
font_pairings.notes: A modern geometric sans with subtly rounded terminals — cleaner than Figtree, warmer than Geist. Versatile across weights. The kind of font that makes everything look considered and premium without trying too hard.

font_pairings.next_font_import:
// Clash Display via next/font/local (fontshare.com)
import { Inter } from 'next/font/google'
font_pairings.notes: A display-first geometric sans with very distinctive uppercase forms. The heavy weights are incredibly impactful for hero text. The light weights are elegant and airy. For when you want the typography itself to be a design statement.

Script font for the logo/brand name creates an intimate, personal feel — like a handwritten letter. Paired with a serif for headings and sans for body. For wellness, therapy, personal services, or any business where the human touch matters more than the corporate brand.

font_pairings.next_font_import:
import { Inter } from 'next/font/google'
// Inter Display via next/font/local (variable font from rsms.me/inter)
font_pairings.notes: Inter Display is optimized for large sizes — slightly tighter spacing, more optical adjustments than regular Inter. When you want the cleanest possible typography without any font personality getting in the way. The content speaks; the font stays invisible. Both Realisting and RealDev use this to let their stunning photography be the star.

color_palettes.notes: Blue communicates trust and reliability. Yellow adds warmth and energy. The most proven SMB service palette — but could also work for a tech startup or a school.
Rich green with light green accents. Feels alive and growing. Works for anything connected to nature, health, or growth — but also a bold choice for finance or education.
Burgundy/mauve on clean off-white. Feels warm and calming without being clinical. Great for any business where trust and personal connection matter.
Near-black with electric lime. Feels expensive and intentional. The lime pops dramatically against dark backgrounds. Bold choice for any business that wants to feel premium and different.
Clean white canvas with a single, powerful orange accent. The restraint makes the orange hit harder. For any business with confidence and a strong visual identity.
Pure black background with white text and red accents. Minimal palette, maximum impact. The red cursor/dot is a signature element. For any business that wants to feel exclusive.
Deep navy/purple with vibrant purple accents. Multi-color system with blues, purples, and greens. Feels intelligent and sophisticated.
Soft lavender background with purple CTAs. Feels creative and approachable. The gradient is subtle but adds depth.
Dark forest green on cream/white. Feels established and grounded. The green reads as both professional and natural.
Dark base with warm cream accents. Multiple accent colors used sparingly. The warm tones on dark background create an editorial, magazine-like feel.
Light blue sky gradients fading to white. Cloud/sky imagery enhances the airy feel. Green CTAs pop against the blue. Incredibly inviting.
Dark background with warm coral/orange accents. The warmth of the accents prevents the dark theme from feeling cold or sterile.
Single powerful blue on white. Virgil Abloh's signature. Proves that one bold color + black + white is all you need.
Deep navy with purple accent. The gold standard for 'trust + premium tech.' Gradient adds subtle depth.
Warm copper tones on cream. Feels hand-crafted and intentional. Like walking into a well-designed office.
Purple on dark background. The classic 'AI/tech' palette. Creates an innovative, forward-looking feel.
Lighter purple on lavender background. Softer than Xtract purple. Feels more consumer-friendly and inviting.
High-contrast green on white. Maximum energy. Feels alive and exciting.
Single bold orange on white. Minimal and confident. The warmth of orange is more approachable than red.
Warm cream background with red accent. Feels nostalgic and cozy. The cream background is warmer than pure white.

Off-white with sage green accents. The muted green feels organic and trustworthy — like a dermatologist's office, not a pharmacy. Great for health, beauty, wellness, or any business that wants to feel clean and considered. The 3D product renders pop beautifully against this backdrop.

Dark forest green with warm cream text and gold accents. Like being inside a luxury forest cabin at night. The warmth of the cream/gold prevents the dark green from feeling cold. Incredible for retreats, hospitality, spas, or any business where the environment IS the product.

Warm cream/ivory background with near-black text and gold accents. The cream is warmer than pure white — it feels like quality paper. Used on two of the most exceptional real estate sites. Works for any business that deals in premium physical spaces or products.

Deep emerald green background with burnt orange accents and warm cream text. The dark green evokes natural ingredients while the orange stimulates appetite. A color palette that makes food photography look incredible. Also works for bars, coffee shops, or premium grocery.

Clean white with a single powerful red-orange accent. The red creates urgency and energy — 'Get Started Now' hits different in vermillion. Works for services where speed and reliability matter (HVAC, emergency services, delivery) but also creative agencies that want to feel bold.

Sandy/warm white with muted gold-brown accents. Feels like raw linen and untreated wood. The entire palette is warm neutrals — no cold tones anywhere. Perfect for design studios, architecture firms, furniture, or any business where materials and craftsmanship matter.

White background with multiple primary-color accents (red, green, yellow). The combination of bold primaries on white is universally fun and approachable. Great for camps, kids' activities, family businesses, events, or anything that should feel joyful and accessible.

Deep midnight navy with gold accents and white text. The gold on navy feels inherently luxurious — like a yacht club membership card. Works for any luxury service, premium automotive, high-end hospitality, or adventure experiences where the premium positioning matters.

heroes.name: Full-Screen Video Background
heroes.description: Full-viewport video playing behind bold text. Cinematic, immersive. The video provides motion without requiring user interaction. Text is minimal — the video does the talking.

implementation.notes: Use object-fit: cover. Add a dark overlay (bg-black/40) for text readability. Video should be compressed to under 5MB for performance.

heroes.name: Large Service Photo + CTA Box Overlay
heroes.description: Full-width background photo of the service or product. Minimal bold text. A prominent action box (quote form, booking CTA) overlaid on the image. Can't miss the CTA.

implementation.html: relative container with bg-cover image, absolute positioned card/form with bg-white shadow-lg
implementation.notes: The overlay card should have enough opacity/shadow to be clearly readable. Keep text to under 10 words. CTA should be high-contrast.

heroes.name: Dark Background + Animated Text Sliding Bar
heroes.description: Dark or image background with text that slides/scrolls in a horizontal bar. Rotating or animated elements (icons, badges). Bold display font for the main headline.

implementation.notes: Use Framer Motion animateX for the sliding bar. Rotating elements via Framer Motion rotate animation. Film grain overlay optional for texture.

heroes.name: Massive Colored Text Panning In Over Photo
heroes.description: Oversized brand/business name text animates in (pans from side) over a bold background photo. Movie-trailer energy. The text IS the design element.

implementation.notes: Framer Motion initial={{ x: -200, opacity: 0 }} animate={{ x: 0, opacity: 1 }} with a large font-size (8-12vw). Background image with object-fit cover.

heroes.name: 3D Product/Dashboard Moving Toward You
heroes.description: A product mockup or dashboard in perspective that translates toward the user on scroll. Cloud/sky gradient background. Feels like the product is emerging from the screen.

implementation.notes: CSS perspective + transform: translateZ() linked to scroll position via Framer Motion useScroll + useTransform. Start with scale(0.8) translateZ(-100px) and animate to scale(1) translateZ(0).

heroes.name: 3D Particle Animation + Self-Writing Text
heroes.description: Animated 3D dots/particles in the background. Large text that writes/types itself as user scrolls. 3D blocks or geometric shapes parallaxing on the side. The most technically impressive hero pattern.

implementation.notes: Three.js or canvas for particle system. Framer Motion useScroll for text reveal (clip-path or character-by-character). 3D blocks via CSS transforms with parallax offset.

heroes.name: Contained Card Hero with Photo + Rating
heroes.description: Hero content inside a rounded card/container with a background color. Professional photo inside the card. Star rating or trust badge prominently displayed. The card sits on a white/light page — it feels designed, not default.

implementation.notes: rounded-2xl overflow-hidden with bg-[brand-color]. Image with object-cover on one side. Star rating component with yellow stars. White text on colored background.

heroes.name: Product Mockups Assembling Together
heroes.description: Multiple UI elements, browser windows, or product screenshots that animate together into a cohesive composition. Pieces come from different directions and assemble like a puzzle.

implementation.notes: Multiple Framer Motion elements with staggered animations. Each piece has different initial positions (x, y, rotation) and animates to final position. Slight overlap creates depth.

heroes.name: Text That Types Itself as You Scroll
heroes.description: Hero text characters appear one by one as the user scrolls, like someone is typing in real time. Creates a narrative, story-telling feel. Engaging and interactive.

implementation.notes: Framer Motion useScroll to track progress. Map scroll progress to character count. Display characters 0..N where N = scrollProgress * totalChars. CSS blink cursor animation: @keyframes blink { 0%-50% opacity: 1, 51%-100% opacity: 0 }

heroes.name: Warm Photo + Floating Tags
heroes.description: Portrait or lifestyle photo with small tag/label elements floating around it (like Convenient, Caring, Confidential). Soft colors, mission statement text alongside. Calming and personal.

implementation.notes: Photo with relative positioning. Tags as absolute-positioned elements with Framer Motion float animation (subtle y oscillation). Tags can have rounded-full bg-primary/10 text-primary styling.

heroes.name: Clean Color Block + Service Photo + Clear CTA
heroes.description: Solid color background (blue, green, any brand color). Service professional photo framed in a contrasting color block (yellow square, white card). Bold clear headline. Big CTA button. Simple and effective.

implementation.notes: Split layout: text on left (2/3), photo on right (1/3) in a colored frame. bg-primary text-white for the section. CTA button in accent color. Very achievable with basic Tailwind.

heroes.name: Stars Rating + Name + Horizontal Gallery Strip
heroes.description: Clean white hero with star rating prominently displayed, business name and tagline, a CTA button, and a horizontal strip of photos/gallery across the bottom of the hero section.

implementation.notes: Stars as a row of SVG star icons. Gallery strip as overflow-x-auto flex gap-4 with images. Or CSS scroll-snap for smooth carousel behavior.

heroes.name: Editorial Asymmetric Grid Hero
heroes.description: Content arranged in an asymmetric editorial grid — different sized blocks of text, images, and whitespace. Feels like a magazine spread. Strong typographic hierarchy.

implementation.notes: CSS Grid with named areas and asymmetric column/row spans. Mix of font sizes (display + caption). Generous whitespace between elements.

heroes.name: Product Icon That Follows You Down the Page
heroes.description: A 3D-rendered product (skin cream jar, shoe, tool) physically moves down the page as you scroll, appearing at different positions in different contexts. The product IS the visual thread tying the entire page together. Exceptionally engaging — the user can't forget what's being sold.

implementation.notes: Position the product with position: fixed or position: sticky. Use Framer Motion useScroll to track page progress. Map scrollYProgress to translate coordinates, scale, and rotation. The product should appear in 3-5 different 'stations' as the user scrolls. Each station has different styling/context. Requires high-quality 3D render or PNG cutout with transparency.

heroes.name: Blurred Background That Clears on Scroll
heroes.description: Huge bold text (buy. sell. rent.) on a blurred/dark background photo that progressively becomes clearer and more transparent as user scrolls down. Creates intrigue, then reveal. The blur-to-clear transition draws you in.

implementation.notes: Background image with CSS filter: blur(Npx). Framer Motion useScroll + useTransform to map scrollYProgress to blur value (from 20px to 0) and opacity (from 0.3 to 1). Text on top with z-index. Text can also fade/scale as user scrolls past it.

heroes.name: Cinematic Timelapse Video Background
heroes.description: High-quality construction/process timelapse video playing behind minimal text. The speed-up creates energy and implies progress and transformation. More dynamic than static video. User called this 'simply amazing.'

implementation.notes: Same as fullscreen-video-hero but the video content is a timelapse. Key difference: timelapse videos are shorter, punchier, and show transformation — perfect for construction, manufacturing, renovation, or any 'before/after' business. Compress to WebM + MP4 fallback, keep under 8MB. Dark overlay for text readability.

heroes.name: Full-Screen Nature Photo Hero
heroes.description: Massive nature/environment photo fills entire viewport. Small availability badge ('5 spots left for November'). Script or serif heading. CTA button. Photo does all the talking — the business IS the environment. Exceptionally powerful for place-based businesses.

implementation.notes: Full-viewport hero with object-cover image. Small badge component (rounded-full bg-white/80 text-sm) for urgency/scarcity. Script font for logo/heading creates intimacy. Keep text to absolute minimum — let the image work. CTA in a warm accent color.

heroes.name: Giant Brand Name Typography Over Product
heroes.description: Business name in enormous letters (filling viewport width) overlaid on or behind a product photo. The typography IS the design. Nordiq has 'NORDIQ' in massive sans filling the viewport with a chair in the 'Q'. Mobius has 'Möbius®' spanning the bottom. Minimal everything else.

implementation.notes: Font-size: 15-25vw for the massive text. Use mix-blend-mode or z-index layering to weave the text with the product image. The product can sit 'inside' a letter or float over the text. Requires careful composition — the font choice matters enormously at this scale. Works best with geometric or high-contrast sans-serif.

heroes.name: Hero with Draggable/Flowing Image Cards
heroes.description: Image portfolio cards that users can drag across the screen or that auto-flow horizontally. Dotted background pattern. Italic accent words in title. Interactive from the first second — users engage immediately by dragging cards.

implementation.notes: Framer Motion drag prop on each card: <motion.div drag='x' dragConstraints={{ left: -500, right: 500 }}>. Cards positioned in a row with overflow visible. Dotted background via CSS radial-gradient. Title with specific words in italic (<em>) and possibly a different color. Stars/rating badge above title.

sections.name: Service Cards with Icons AND Photos
sections.description: Grid of service cards where each card has both an icon and a photo. Visual redundancy helps users scan quickly. Clean titles and brief descriptions.

sections.name: Alternating Text/Image Service Rows
sections.description: Services displayed in alternating rows — text left / image right, then image left / text right. Each service has a numbered list of sub-items (01, 02, 03...) in monospace. Creates visual rhythm.

sections.name: Dark Interactive Service Cards
sections.description: Dark cards with interactive elements per service. Typing animations, dynamic counters, moving elements. Each card feels alive.

sections.name: Scroll-Pinned Card Cascade
sections.description: The section stays pinned to the viewport while service cards cascade/slide through it as the user scrolls. The page doesn't move — only the cards change. Incredibly immersive.

implementation.notes: position: sticky on the section container. Height set to N * 100vh (where N = number of cards). Cards absolutely positioned and animated via Framer Motion useScroll with offset breakpoints.

sections.name: Simple Color Rectangle Cards
sections.description: Clean rectangular cards with consistent padding, subtle background color, service title, and brief description. Minimal decoration. The simplicity IS the design.

sections.name: Numbered Steps with Image Cards
sections.description: 3-4 numbered steps, each with an image card showing that step being performed. Numbers are large and prominent. Builds confidence by showing exactly how it works.

sections.name: Numbered Tabs with Full-Width Photos
sections.description: Process steps as numbered tabs at the top (01 Discover, 02 Select, 03 Experience, 04 Return). Clicking/scrolling each tab reveals a full-width photo and description for that step.

sections.name: Steps Rotating Around a Globe/Arc
sections.description: Process steps orbit around a central globe or arc graphic as the user scrolls. Each step appears at a different position around the circle. Scroll-driven rotation.

sections.name: Numbered Steps with Hand-Drawn Connectors
sections.description: Simple 1-2-3 numbered process with hand-drawn arrow SVGs connecting the steps. Feels personal and approachable, not corporate.

sections.name: Featured Large Testimonial + Smaller Cards
sections.description: One large, featured testimonial with a big photo at the top. Below it, a grid or row of smaller testimonial cards with avatars. Creates hierarchy — one star review, plus supporting voices.

sections.name: Horizontally Auto-Scrolling Colored Boxes
sections.description: Testimonial cards in colored boxes that auto-scroll horizontally. The color of the boxes matches the brand palette. Creates continuous motion — the section feels alive.

sections.name: Dark Cards with Large Quote Marks
sections.description: Dark background cards with oversized quote mark decorations (" "). Client name and role below. Cards can be in a horizontal carousel.

sections.name: Star Rating Review Cards
sections.description: White cards with star ratings (gold stars), review text, and reviewer name. Clean and familiar — looks like Google/Yelp reviews embedded on the site.

sections.name: Dark Cards with Large Numbers
sections.description: Row of dark/black cards, each with a large white number ($2.8M, 120K, 200,000+) and a label below. Numbers animate/count up when scrolled into view.

sections.name: Light Background Counter Row
sections.description: Large numbers on a light/white background in a horizontal row. Numbers count up from 0 with animated counting. Labels below each number.

sections.name: With Us vs Without Us Comparison
sections.description: Side-by-side table comparing 'Other options' vs 'Working with us'. One side has X marks (red/gray), the other has checkmarks (green/brand color). Powerful conversion tool.

sections.name: Team Photos with Credential Tags
sections.description: Row of portrait photos with names, handwritten-style or serif font names, and small tag/label components showing specializations or credentials. Users can quickly scan to find the right person.

sections.name: Warm Portrait Photo Row on Dark Background
sections.description: Row of warm, well-lit portrait photos on a dark background. Names and roles below. The warm lighting contrasts with the dark bg — people look approachable and real.

sections.name: Colored Numbered Accordion FAQ
sections.description: FAQ accordion where each item has a numbered label (001, 002...) and sits on a colored background (brand accent color). Feels designed, not default. The numbers add order and scanability.

sections.name: Clean Minimal Accordion FAQ
sections.description: Simple question/answer accordion with clean typography and minimal decoration. Plus/minus or chevron toggle icon. The questions are the design — no visual noise.

sections.name: Aesthetic Image Grid
sections.description: 6-up or 9-up image grid with consistent spacing. Images may have hover effects (slight zoom, overlay). CSS Grid auto-fill with minmax for responsiveness.

implementation.notes: Images with aspect-ratio: 4/3. Hover: scale-105 opacity-90 transition. Use next/image with fill and object-cover.

sections.name: Horizontal Scrolling Image Gallery
sections.description: Full-width horizontal scrolling gallery of images. Can be auto-scrolling or manual. Images peek from the edges to indicate more content.

implementation.notes: Each image as snap-start. Hide scrollbar with scrollbar-hide utility. Optional: CSS scroll-snap for smooth snapping.

sections.name: Modular Overlapping Project Cards
sections.description: Project/portfolio cards with mixed light and dark backgrounds that slightly overlap each other. Different sizes create visual hierarchy. Feels curated and editorial.

sections.name: Product Grid with Specs and Pricing
sections.description: Grid of product cards on dark background with studio-quality photos. Each card shows specs (size, power, type) and pricing. Clean labels, consistent layout.

sections.name: Asymmetric Blog Card Grid
sections.description: Blog section with one large featured card (with photo, title, author, tag) and 2-3 smaller cards below/beside it. Category tags in colored pills.

sections.name: Industry/Service Tag Grid
sections.description: Grid of industry or service categories as tag-like boxes with icons. Colored background. Each tag is clickable or hoverable. Shows breadth of expertise at a glance.

sections.name: Overlapping Rectangular Sections
sections.description: Content sections that literally cover each other up as you scroll. Each section slides over the previous one at a different scroll speed. Creates a 'layered paper' depth effect.

implementation.notes: position: sticky on each section. Increasing z-index per section. Framer Motion translateY at different rates per section. Background color per section to cover the previous.

sections.name: Full-Width Mission Statement CTA
sections.description: Large serif text with a mission statement or call to action. Centered. Generous whitespace above and below. A single prominent CTA button. Simple and powerful.

sections.name: Oversized Logo Footer
sections.description: Footer with a massive version of the logo/business name as the dominant visual element. Navigation links and contact info are secondary. The logo anchors the end of the page.

sections.name: Scaling Footer Takeover
sections.description: The footer section scales up from small to fill the viewport as you scroll to the bottom. Creates an immersive ending — the website 'opens up' at the end.

implementation.notes: Framer Motion useScroll with transform: scale() going from 0.5 to 1.0 based on scroll position near bottom of page.

sections.name: Partner/Client Logo Bar with Hover Effects
sections.description: Row of partner or client logos, typically grayscale, that gain color or subtle animation on hover. Shows credibility at a glance. 'We've partnered with' heading above.

implementation.css: filter grayscale(100%) opacity-60 hover:grayscale(0) hover:opacity-100 transition-all duration-300
implementation.notes: Logos in a flex row with gap. Grayscale by default, full color on hover. Can also auto-scroll as a marquee for many logos.

sections.name: Rotating Team Image Carousel
sections.description: Team member photos in a rotating bar/carousel that auto-cycles through team members. Each rotation reveals a new face. More dynamic than a static grid.

sections.name: Proven Process Methodology Layout
sections.description: Step-by-step methodology display that shows how the business works — positioned as an educational journey. Different from simple numbered steps — this feels like a strategic framework with descriptions, icons, and a visual flow connecting them.

sections.name: Modular Product Parts Snapping Into Place
sections.description: Product/work showcase where individual parts (cards, mockups, screenshots) fade in and snap into position with a modular, component-based feel. Each piece appears independent but assembles into a cohesive layout.

implementation.notes: Framer Motion staggered entrance with each element having slightly different initial position/rotation. Use spring transitions for the snapping feel. Layout with CSS Grid for final positions.

sections.name: Flowing Analytics Charts & Data Visualizations
sections.description: Multiple chart/visualization components that animate in concert — bars grow, lines draw, numbers count, all synchronized. Creates a 'living dashboard' feel. The most visually complex section pattern found.

implementation.notes: SVG charts with stroke-dashoffset animation for line drawing. Bar heights animated with Framer Motion. All triggered by intersection observer. Staggered timing creates the 'flowing' feel.

sections.name: Beautifully Designed Pricing Cards
sections.description: 3-tier pricing section with visually distinct cards. The recommended tier is highlighted with a different color or larger card. Clean typography, clear feature lists, prominent CTA per tier. Not just functional — designed to be beautiful.

implementation.notes: 3 cards in a flex/grid row. Middle card slightly larger (scale-105) with primary color bg or border. Feature list with checkmarks. Monthly/yearly toggle optional. CTA button per card.

sections.name: Tool Integrations Flowing In Sequentially
sections.description: Integration partner logos or tool icons that flow/animate into view one by one in a beautiful sequential entrance. Creates a feeling of an ecosystem coming together.

implementation.notes: Framer Motion staggerChildren with each logo having initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 20 }} animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}. Stagger delay of 0.05-0.1s per item.

sections.name: Text/Elements Moving Spatially Through Section
sections.description: A text element or visual that physically moves through the section space as you scroll — like 'Buyers' text moving down the screen in a voice assistant demo. Creates spatial storytelling.

implementation.notes: Framer Motion useScroll + useTransform to map scroll progress to translateY of the moving element. The element moves within a fixed-height container.

sections.name: Cinematic Preview Card (Movie Theater Feel)
sections.description: A large card that floats over the hero content with a 'Design that captivates today and inspires tomorrow' type message. Feels like a movie theater preview card — dramatic framing, centered, with a slight shadow/glow.

sections.name: Rectangular Elements Panning In From Sides on Scroll
sections.description: Large rectangular cards or components slide in from the left or right side of the viewport as you scroll. Each new element takes over the previous one. Creates a 'flipping through a portfolio' feel.

implementation.notes: Framer Motion useScroll + useTransform. Map scroll progress to translateX from ±100vw to 0. Alternate left/right per element.

sections.name: Section Expands to Fill Entire Viewport
sections.description: A section starts as a contained card/block and expands to fill the entire viewport as you scroll into it. Big text fills the screen. Creates an immersive moment mid-page, not just at the end.

implementation.notes: Framer Motion useScroll + useTransform. Map scroll progress to: width from max-w-4xl to 100vw, padding from px-8 to px-0, borderRadius from 2xl to 0. Content scales up inside.

sections.name: Class/Appointment Schedule Table
sections.description: Clean, scannable table showing class times, appointment slots, or service schedules. Day/time grid format. Color-coded by type. Essential for any appointment-based business.

implementation.notes: HTML table or CSS Grid. Columns for days, rows for time slots. Color-coded pills for class types. Responsive: stack to a list on mobile. hover:bg-primary/5 for row highlighting.

sections.name: Designed Location Map Integration
sections.description: An embedded map that's designed into the page — not just a dropped-in Google Maps iframe. Custom styling, brand-colored pins, integrated with surrounding content (address, hours, directions). Signals professionalism.

implementation.notes: Google Maps embed with custom styling (snazzy maps or Maps JS API with custom theme). Or static map image with a 'Get Directions' link. Frame with rounded corners and shadow to match site aesthetic.

sections.name: Animated Diagram/Flowchart
sections.description: Process or architecture diagrams that animate on scroll — lines draw, nodes appear, connections form. Shows relationships between elements visually rather than just describing them.

implementation.notes: SVG paths with stroke-dasharray + stroke-dashoffset animation. Nodes fade in with staggered timing. Lines draw between nodes as scroll progresses.

sections.name: Why Choose Us Checklist Format
sections.description: A 'Why Choose Us' section presented as a checklist rather than a grid of cards. Each point has a checkmark, interesting text styling, and possibly icons. Scannable and persuasive.

implementation.notes: Unordered list with custom checkmark icons (lucide-react Check). Each item with bold lead text + lighter description. Alternating subtle background colors optional.

sections.name: Scroll-Away Feature Reasons
sections.description: Features/reasons displayed one at a time, each scrolling away to reveal the next. 'Five ingredients, nothing more' → scroll → next reason appears. Full-viewport storytelling. Each reason gets the entire screen. The user's attention is captured one point at a time.

implementation.notes: Each reason is a full-viewport (h-screen) sticky section. Use Framer Motion useScroll with offset breakpoints to control which reason is visible. Total container height = N * 100vh. Opacity and translateY transitions between reasons. Keep text minimal per reason — one powerful statement + supporting paragraph.

sections.name: Step Process with Image Fade-Away
sections.description: Steps 1-2-3 displayed next to a heading ('Your new skincare routine is beautifully simple'). Each step's image fades into/covers the previous one as you scroll or click. The transition IS the navigation — watching the image morph from step to step is the experience.

implementation.notes: Split layout: text steps on left, image frame on right. Use AnimatePresence with Framer Motion to crossfade images. Steps can auto-advance on scroll (useScroll) or be clickable tabs. Each step has: step number, title, brief description. Image container with overflow: hidden and smooth opacity transitions.

sections.name: E-commerce Product Unboxing Layout
sections.description: Product shown inside its packaging/box with size toggles (Standard 50ml / Travel 20ml), original vs sale price, and 'Add to Bag' CTA. The unboxing presentation makes the product feel premium — you can almost feel the packaging.

implementation.notes: Split layout: product image (inside open box) on left, product details on right. Size selector as pill-style toggle buttons. Price with strikethrough on original. Green/muted CTA button. Thumbnails for alternate views on the side. Rounded container with subtle shadow.

sections.name: Process + Materials Split Layout
sections.description: Left column: numbered process steps (01 Sourcing, 02 Design & Proportion, 03 Crafting, 04 Finishing & Assembly) with descriptions. Right column: materials list with botanical/hand-drawn illustrations (Birch, Pine, Oak, Ash) with descriptions. Two parallel narratives on one page.

implementation.notes: CSS Grid with 2 columns on desktop (single column mobile). Left: numbered list with serif headings, body text descriptions. Right: material items with small illustration/icon + name + description. Horizontal dividers between items. Clean serif typography for headings.

sections.name: Geographic Neighborhood Exploration Grid
sections.description: Grid of neighborhood/area photos with location names and arrow icons. Clicking one fills half the screen with a detailed 'flyer' view — almost a mini-site for that area. User called the Brickell flyer 'really nice, almost sexy.' Interactive geographic discovery.

implementation.notes: CSS Grid of location cards with hover effects (slight zoom, overlay). On click: AnimatePresence panel slides in from right covering 50% of viewport. Panel contains: hero image, area name, description, key stats, listing previews, 'View All' CTA. Close button returns to grid. Images should have parallax-lite on scroll (background-position shift).

sections.name: Beautiful Property/Service Submission Form
sections.description: Multi-field form that's so well-designed you WANT to fill it out. Each field has generous spacing, subtle animations, and the overall form feels like a product, not a chore. Fields animate in on focus. The form IS a design element.

implementation.notes: Large input fields with subtle bottom borders (not full boxes). Labels above in muted text, animate to smaller on focus. Generous vertical spacing (space-y-8). Fields fade-up stagger on section entrance. Submit button full-width with brand color. Optional: progress indicator for multi-step forms.

sections.name: Visual Agency/Competitor Comparison
sections.description: Side-by-side comparison with a large, beautiful background image and a checklist overlay. More visual and dramatic than a simple table — the background image adds emotional weight. The image makes you FEEL the difference, not just read it.

implementation.notes: Full-width section with a large background image (object-cover). Dark overlay for readability. Two columns of checklist items floating over the image. Left column: competitor (X marks, muted text). Right column: us (checkmarks, bright text, brand color). The visual context of the bg image reinforces the message.

sections.name: Big Text Restaurant Menu Display
sections.description: Menu in huge, appetizing typography divided into segments (Starters, Mains, Desserts). Menu item names are the design — oversized serif or display type, minimal descriptions. Chef photo with blockquote completes the story. The menu IS the website.

implementation.notes: Menu items in large display font (text-3xl to text-5xl). Price right-aligned on same line. Brief description in smaller muted text below. Category headers in uppercase with decorative rule. Two-column layout for desktop. Chef photo with blockquote in a separate card below menu.

sections.name: Image Cards That Become Videos on Hover/Click
sections.description: Cards showing static images that transition to playing videos when hovered or clicked. User said this 'really levels up a website.' The surprise of motion from a static card is delightful.

implementation.notes: Card with relative positioning. Image visible by default. Video element below image with opacity-0. On hover: image fades out (opacity-0), video fades in (opacity-100) and starts playing. Use onMouseEnter to call video.play() and onMouseLeave to call video.pause(). Video should be muted and looping. Preload='metadata' to avoid loading all videos upfront.

sections.name: Nature-Themed Pricing Highlight
sections.description: Pricing cards where the recommended option is highlighted by a natural element — a leaf sprouting over a forest background to indicate 'most popular.' Thematic, not generic. Much more memorable than a simple 'Most Popular' badge.

implementation.notes: 3 pricing cards. Middle card (recommended) has a unique visual treatment: leaf SVG icon sprouting from the top edge, different background (forest photo with overlay, or just a richer brand color). Other cards have clean/minimal treatment. The contrast makes the recommended option irresistible. Adapt the theme to the business — a restaurant might use a fork, a contractor might use a blueprint.

sections.name: Cards That Zoom In From Below Screen
sections.description: About/feature cards start transparent and positioned below the visible viewport, then zoom into view and become opaque as user scrolls. Dramatic reveal — feels like the content is rising to meet you. User called this 'great.'

implementation.notes: Framer Motion initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 100, scale: 0.8 }} whileInView={{ opacity: 1, y: 0, scale: 1 }} transition={{ duration: 0.8, ease: 'easeOut' }}. Apply to each card with staggered delay. viewport={{ once: true, margin: '-100px' }} to trigger before cards are fully in view.

sections.name: Large Typography Stats with Animation
sections.description: Stats displayed as massive typographic elements (40+ years, 87% on-time delivery) with animated counters and elegant serif/display fonts. The numbers ARE the design — not in cards, but free-floating on the page with generous whitespace. Monumental feel.

implementation.notes: Stats in huge display font (text-8xl to text-9xl). Animated counting via useMotionValue + animate. Each stat on its own horizontal band/row with lots of vertical spacing. Description text in smaller size next to or below the number. Serif or display font for the numbers, sans for descriptions. Optional: plus sign or percent animates in after the count completes.

sections.name: Glassmorphism / Frosted Glass Cards
sections.description: Cards with semi-transparent backgrounds, backdrop blur, and thin borders that create a 'glassy' premium feel. Used for testimonials overlaid on video or image backgrounds — the content behind bleeds through with a frosted effect. User specifically praised Yogus's 'glassy feel and transparent boxes with testimonials.'

implementation.css: backdrop-filter: blur(16px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(16px); background: rgba(255,255,255,0.08); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.15); border-radius: 1rem;
implementation.notes: Works best over video or image backgrounds where the blur creates visible frosting. On dark backgrounds use rgba(255,255,255,0.08). On light backgrounds use rgba(255,255,255,0.6). Add subtle border for definition. Can combine with box-shadow for depth. Ensure fallback for browsers without backdrop-filter support.

sections.name: Sequential Construction/Build Animation
sections.description: Animation showing a property (or product) being built step-by-step — from foundation to finished building. Each scroll increment reveals the next construction phase. User called RealDev's version 'simply stunning.' Can be implemented as a sprite sequence, layered images revealed on scroll, or a controlled video scrub.

implementation.notes: Option 1 (Image sequence): 20-40 images of build stages. useScroll maps scrollYProgress to frame index. Display current frame. Option 2 (Layered reveal): Stack transparent PNGs of each build phase. Each layer fades in at a scroll threshold. Option 3 (Video scrub): Video of construction, currentTime controlled by scroll position (video.currentTime = scrollProgress * video.duration). Option 3 is most impressive but requires a good source video.

sections.name: Decorative Geometric Shape Accents
sections.description: Small geometric shapes (triangles, circles, squares, diamonds) scattered throughout the design as visual accents. They add personality and playfulness without dominating. Suntrail uses colored triangles and circles that 'stand out' as design elements. Can be static or subtly animated.

implementation.notes: Position decorative SVG shapes using absolute positioning. Use brand colors with reduced opacity. Scatter at section transitions and alongside headings. Optional: subtle float animation (translateY oscillation over 3-5s). Keep shapes small (16-32px). Use CSS rotation for variety. Can also be implemented as CSS pseudo-elements (::before, ::after) with clip-path for triangles.

sections.name: Rotating/Cycling Words Display
sections.description: A section of text where one word cycles through alternatives — e.g., 'We create [clarity / imagination / beauty / design]' with each word rotating in on a timer or scroll. Different from 'scattered words assembling' — this is inline word replacement within a sentence. Nordiq uses rotating words in its studio tour section.

implementation.notes: AnimatePresence with mode='wait'. Array of words cycling on a setInterval (2-3s). Each word exits upward with opacity 0, enters from below with opacity 1. Or use Framer Motion layoutId for smooth morphing. CSS overflow: hidden on the word container to clip the animation. Fixed-width container prevents layout shift.

sections.name: Large Text Flowing Across the Screen
sections.description: Large display text that pans/flows horizontally across the screen, often as a decorative or branding element. Bamzi's 'Big Tex flows across the screen nicely.' The text moves continuously or on scroll, creating kinetic energy. Similar to a marquee but with much larger, bolder typography.

implementation.notes: Text in text-6xl to text-9xl with font-bold. Framer Motion animate={{ x: [0, -totalWidth] }} with repeat: Infinity for continuous flow. Or useScroll + useTransform for scroll-driven movement. Multiple lines can move in opposite directions for added dynamism. Use will-change: transform and translateZ(0) for GPU acceleration.

sections.name: Property/Product Detail Page Layout
sections.description: A full detail page layout: large hero image or video at top that hooks you in, followed by descriptive text, specs/features grid, photo gallery, and CTA. RealDev's Orient Sky Penthouse page has 'big image with all the different components' plus 'a video would play and then there's a bunch of words and details at the bottom — hooks you in at the beginning.'

implementation.notes: Structure: (1) Full-width hero image or video (min-h-[60vh]), (2) Title + price + key specs row, (3) Description in max-w-prose, (4) Features grid (2-3 columns), (5) Photo gallery (grid or horizontal scroll), (6) Location/map, (7) CTA section. Each section fades up on scroll. Hero video autoplays muted. On mobile, stack everything single-column.

sections.name: Symmetrical Blog Grid with Panning Images
sections.description: Blog/news section with a consistent, symmetrical card grid. Each card has an image that subtly pans (shifts position) on scroll, creating life and movement across the grid. Different from the 'asymmetric blog cards' pattern — this uses uniform card sizes for a clean, organized look. RealDev uses this with 'consistent images and how they panned out.'

implementation.notes: CSS Grid: grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-6. Each card has overflow-hidden. Image inside with object-cover and a slight translateY transform linked to scroll (useScroll on each card, map to small translateY range like [-20, 20]). This creates subtle parallax within each card. Category tags as colored pills. Consistent card heights via aspect-ratio.

sections.name: Studio Tour / Playable Interactive Content
sections.description: A section showcasing a studio, workspace, or behind-the-scenes content with playable video or interactive elements. Nordiq features 'studio tour with playable content and rotating words' — a section that invites exploration rather than passive scrolling. Combines video, interactive elements, and text.

implementation.notes: Split layout: video/image carousel on one side, descriptive text with rotating keywords on the other. Video plays inline (not fullscreen) with custom play button overlay. Can include a grid of behind-the-scenes photos below. Play button: absolute centered, rounded-full bg-white/80 with Play icon from lucide-react. On click: video.play() and hide button.

animations.name: Fade Up on Scroll
animations.description: Elements fade in and slide up slightly when they enter the viewport. The baseline animation — every site should have this.

implementation.framer_motion: initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 30 }} whileInView={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }} viewport={{ once: true }} transition={{ duration: 0.6 }}
implementation.notes: Apply to every section below the fold. Use viewport={{ once: true }} so it only triggers once.

animations.name: Staggered Children Reveal
animations.description: A group of elements (cards, list items) fade in one after another with a slight delay between each. Creates a cascading effect.

implementation.framer_motion:
Parent: variants={{ hidden: {}, visible: { transition: { staggerChildren: 0.1 } } }} initial='hidden' whileInView='visible'
Child: variants={{ hidden: { opacity: 0, y: 20 }, visible: { opacity: 1, y: 0 } }}

animations.name: Hover Scale on Cards
animations.description: Cards slightly scale up on hover with a smooth transition. Simple but effective interactivity.

animations.name: Horizontal Auto-Scrolling Carousel
animations.description: Content (testimonials, logos, images) auto-scrolls horizontally in an infinite loop. Creates continuous motion — the section feels alive even without interaction.

implementation.notes: Duplicate the content array and use CSS animation: @keyframes scroll { 0% { transform: translateX(0); } 100% { transform: translateX(-50%); } }. animation: scroll 30s linear infinite. Or Framer Motion animate={{ x: [0, -totalWidth/2] }} with repeat: Infinity.

animations.name: Animated Number Counter
animations.description: Numbers count up from 0 to their target value when scrolled into view. Works whenever you have impressive stats. Framer Motion or simple requestAnimationFrame.

implementation.framer_motion: useMotionValue(0) + useTransform to format. Trigger with useInView. animate(motionValue, targetNumber, { duration: 2 }).
implementation.notes: Format with toLocaleString() for commas. Add + or % suffix after the number.

animations.name: Decorative Dot Pattern Background
animations.description: Subtle dot pattern as a background texture. Adds visual interest without distraction. Can be CSS radial-gradient or SVG.

animations.name: Film Grain Noise Overlay
animations.description: Subtle noise texture overlay on hero or full page. Creates a warm, analog, printed feel. Adds tactile quality to flat digital surfaces.

implementation.css: .grain::after { content: ''; position: fixed; inset: 0; background: url('/noise.png'); mix-blend-mode: hard-light; opacity: 0.03; pointer-events: none; z-index: 9999; }

animations.name: Scroll-Pinned Section with Changing Content
animations.description: A section pins to the viewport while internal content (cards, images, text) animates through as the user scrolls. The page appears to stop scrolling while the content changes. Incredibly immersive.

implementation.notes: Outer container height: N * 100vh. Inner container: position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100vh; overflow: hidden. Use Framer Motion useScroll with container ref to track progress within the section. Map progress to which card is visible.

animations.name: Sections That Cover Each Other on Scroll
animations.description: Each content section has position: sticky and slides over the previous section as you scroll. Creates a layered, stacking effect — like shuffling through a deck of cards.

implementation.notes: Each section: position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: N (increasing). Each section needs a solid background color to cover the previous. Framer Motion can add subtle scale/rotation transforms per section.

animations.name: 3D Perspective Movement on Scroll
animations.description: An element moves in 3D space (toward the user) as they scroll. Uses CSS perspective and translateZ. Creates a dramatic depth effect.

implementation.framer_motion: useScroll + useTransform to map scrollYProgress to translateZ value. Start at translateZ(-200px) rotateX(10deg) and animate to translateZ(0) rotateX(0).

animations.name: Zoom Out Reveal on Scroll
animations.description: An image or mockup starts zoomed in (scale > 1) and scales down as the user scrolls, gradually revealing the full picture. Satisfying reveal effect.

implementation.framer_motion: useScroll + useTransform to map scrollYProgress to scale. From scale(1.5) to scale(1). Optional: also map to borderRadius change.

animations.name: Text That Types Itself on Scroll
animations.description: Characters appear one by one as the user scrolls, like someone is typing. Creates a narrative, story-telling feel. Engaging and interactive.

implementation.notes: Framer Motion useScroll to track progress. Map scrollYProgress (0-1) to character count (0-totalChars). Render text.substring(0, visibleChars). Add CSS blinking cursor: @keyframes blink { 0%,50% { opacity: 1 } 51%,100% { opacity: 0 } }

animations.name: Alternating Direction Row Scroll
animations.description: Multiple rows of text/items where odd rows scroll left and even rows scroll right (or vice versa). Creates a dynamic, kinetic feeling.

implementation.framer_motion: useScroll + useTransform. Odd rows: translateX maps from 0 to -100. Even rows: translateX maps from 0 to 100. Creates a spreading/diverging effect.

animations.name: Process Steps Orbiting a Central Element
animations.description: Process steps positioned around a central circle/globe. As the user scrolls, the active step rotates around the circle. Scroll-driven rotation transform.

implementation.notes: Central element with position: relative. Steps positioned with transform: rotate(Ndeg) translateX(radius) rotate(-Ndeg). Framer Motion useScroll maps progress to the rotation angle.

animations.name: Element Scales Up to Fill Viewport
animations.description: A section or element starts small and scales up to fill the entire viewport as the user scrolls to it. Dramatic, immersive ending effect.

implementation.framer_motion: useScroll with target ref. useTransform to map scrollYProgress to scale from 0.5 to 1.0. Also map to borderRadius from '2rem' to '0rem' for a rounded-to-fullscreen effect.

animations.name: 3D Particle/Dot Animation Background
animations.description: Animated dots/particles floating in 3D space behind the content. Creates depth and visual interest without distracting from the content. Can use Three.js, canvas, or pure CSS.

implementation.notes: Lightweight option: CSS dots with different animation-duration values for parallax effect. Medium: Canvas 2D with requestAnimationFrame. Heavy: Three.js with BufferGeometry points. Always check performance — particles should never make the page lag.

animations.name: Marquee/Ticker Scrolling Text
animations.description: Text or logos scrolling continuously in a marquee/ticker style. Can be single or multi-row. Infinite scroll creates rhythm and movement.

implementation.css:
@keyframes marquee { 0% { transform: translateX(0); } 100% { transform: translateX(-50%); } }
.marquee { animation: marquee 20s linear infinite; }
implementation.notes: Duplicate content to create seamless loop. Use will-change: transform for GPU acceleration. Pause on hover with animation-play-state: paused.

animations.name: Custom Cursor / Scroll Indicator
animations.description: Replace the default cursor with a custom element (colored dot, branded circle). Can grow/shrink on hover. Creates a premium, designed feel.

implementation.notes: Div following mouse via onMouseMove → setState. Framer Motion for smooth trailing: animate={{ x: mouseX, y: mouseY }} with spring transition. Mix-blend-mode: difference for invert effect.

animations.name: Split-Flap Display Counter
animations.description: Retro split-flap airport-style number display. Numbers flip mechanically. Creates a nostalgic, tactile feel.

implementation.notes: Each digit has top and bottom halves. CSS rotateX(90deg) on the flipping half. TransformOrigin: bottom for top half flip, top for bottom half flip. Sequential animation with staggered delays.

animations.name: Gradient Color Transitions Between Sections
animations.description: Background color subtly shifts via gradient transitions as user scrolls between sections. Creates a fluid, connected feel where the page breathes with color rather than having hard section breaks. DRAFTR uses lavender-to-deeper-purple transitions with animated elements inside each gradient zone.

implementation.notes: Use CSS linear-gradient backgrounds on sections with overlapping colors at boundaries. Framer Motion useScroll + useTransform to interpolate background-color based on scroll position. Or simpler: each section has a gradient bg that naturally flows into the next section's gradient start color.

animations.name: Product Element Following Scroll Position
animations.description: A 3D product render physically tracks the user's scroll position, appearing at different places on the page in different contexts. The product moves from the hero → features section → testimonials → CTA, serving as a visual thread.

implementation.notes: Product image with position: fixed. Framer Motion useScroll to get scrollYProgress for the full page. Map scrollYProgress to an array of positions (translateX, translateY, scale, rotation) using useTransform with breakpoints. Each breakpoint = a 'station' where the product rests. Use will-change: transform for performance. The product PNG needs transparent background.

animations.name: Sentence That Writes Itself (Ambient/Timed)
animations.description: Text appears character by character as if being typed, auto-playing on a timer (not tied to scroll). 'Five proven ingredients that actually work. Less bottles. Better skin.' Different from scroll-typing — this is ambient and plays when the section enters view.

implementation.notes: Use Framer Motion animate with a custom variant that maps to text length. On whileInView trigger, animate a counter from 0 to text.length over N seconds. Display text.substring(0, counter). Add a blinking cursor span after the last character. Pause briefly between sentences (detect periods). Can chain multiple sentences with delays.

animations.name: Images Sliding in Opposite Directions
animations.description: Multiple images on a page animate in from opposite sides simultaneously — some from left, some from right. Creates a dynamic, converging energy. The collision of opposing motions is visually exciting.

implementation.notes: Alternate images between initial={{ x: -100, opacity: 0 }} and initial={{ x: 100, opacity: 0 }}. Odd items from left, even from right (or vice versa). whileInView={{ x: 0, opacity: 1 }}. Stagger with 0.1-0.2s delay. Creates a satisfying convergence when multiple images slide in simultaneously.

animations.name: Scroll-Driven Story Reveal with Waving Images
animations.description: As user scrolls, story sentences appear one by one while images 'wave' in and out from the sides at different parallax rates. The about section becomes a cinematic narrative experience. User called RealDev's version 'simply amazing.'

implementation.notes: Container with height: 300-500vh for scroll distance. position: sticky inner content. useScroll to track progress. Sentences mapped to scroll ranges (0-0.2 = sentence 1, 0.2-0.4 = sentence 2, etc.). Images with different useTransform rates for parallax — some enter from left, some from right, at different speeds. Opacity tied to scroll position. Each sentence fades in as previous fades. The key is the IMAGES having personality — they wave, rotate slightly, scale.

animations.name: Product 360° Rotation on Scroll
animations.description: A product (furniture, car, artifact) appears to rotate as user scrolls, showing it from multiple angles. Can use a sprite sheet of pre-rendered angles or CSS 3D transforms on a single image.

implementation.notes: Option 1 (sprite sheet): Sequence of 24-36 images at different angles. useScroll maps to frame index. Display the correct frame image. Option 2 (3D CSS): perspective + rotateY transform linked to scroll. Option 3 (Three.js): Load GLTF model, rotate on scroll. For most SMB sites, Option 1 with high-quality product photos is the best balance of quality vs. complexity.

animations.name: Words Scattered Then Assembling
animations.description: Individual words ('clarity', 'imagination', 'beauty', 'design') scattered across the viewport at random positions and sizes, then assembling into a coherent sentence or layout as user scrolls or after a time delay.

implementation.notes: Each word as a Framer Motion element with initial position scattered (random x, y coordinates across viewport). On scroll or timer trigger, animate all words to their final positions (forming a sentence or grid). Use spring transitions for organic movement. The words should feel like they're 'finding their place.' Font size can also change during animation.

animations.name: Product Video Synced with Moving Text
animations.description: A video plays while text elements move in coordination — words flow alongside the video content. Mobius uses this to create a unified narrative where video and typography are one system, not separate elements.

implementation.notes: Video element with currentTime controlled by scroll position (useScroll → video.currentTime = progress * duration). Text elements positioned absolutely and animated with the same scroll progress. Key: both video and text share the same timing source (scroll position), creating perfect sync. Requires careful choreography — map out what text appears at what video timestamp.

navigation.name: Minimal Sticky Nav with CTA Button
navigation.description: Logo on left, 3-4 links centered or right, prominent CTA button (Get a Quote, Book Now). Sticky on scroll. The most common and effective pattern.

navigation.name: Full Navigation on Dark Background
navigation.description: 6-8 navigation links on a dark background. White text. CTA button in accent color. Works with dark-themed sites.

navigation.name: Navigation Inside Contained Hero Card
navigation.description: Nav sits inside the hero's bounded card/container rather than spanning full width. Creates a cohesive, designed unit.

navigation.name: Full-Screen Overlay Menu
navigation.description: Hamburger icon that opens a full-screen overlay menu. Large text links. Dark or branded background. Dramatic and immersive.

navigation.name: Navigation with Live Time/Location
navigation.description: Nav includes a live clock or location indicator (e.g., 'London 4:33PM'). Adds a personal, real-time touch. Small detail, big personality.

navigation.name: Navigation with Scrolling Announcement Banner
navigation.description: Top marquee banner scrolling promotions/announcements above the main nav. 'Breathe Easy — Duct Cleaning 25% Off This Month' type messages auto-scrolling. Dual-purpose: navigation + promotion. Creates urgency.

navigation.name: Centered Logo with Split Navigation
navigation.description: Logo centered in the navigation bar with links split evenly on both sides. Feels balanced and premium — symmetry creates elegance. Works especially well when the brand name/logo is a strong visual element.

interactions.name: Mix Blend Mode on Hover
interactions.description: Images or cards use mix-blend-mode on hover to create color-shifting effects. Difference, multiply, or overlay modes create unexpected visual combinations.

interactions.name: Custom Text Selection Colors
interactions.description: Override the default blue text selection with brand colors. Small detail that shows attention to design.

interactions.name: Smooth Scroll to Sections
interactions.description: Clicking nav links smoothly scrolls to the corresponding section. CSS scroll-behavior or JS smooth scroll.

implementation.notes: Add scroll-margin-top to sections to account for sticky nav height.

interactions.name: Hover to Reveal Additional Content
interactions.description: Cards or images reveal additional content (description, CTA, details) on hover. Content slides up or fades in.

implementation.css: group/card relative overflow-hidden. Inner content: translate-y-full group-hover/card:translate-y-0 transition-transform duration-300

interactions.name: Parallax Image on Scroll
interactions.description: Background images move at a slower rate than the page scroll, creating depth. Simple but effective.

implementation.framer_motion: useScroll + useTransform to map scrollY to a slower translateY value on the image.

interactions.name: Click-Through Preview Icons on Products
interactions.description: Small 'view preview' icons on product/portfolio cards that let you click through different views/angles without leaving the page. Inline product exploration — hover reveals a play/eye icon, clicking cycles through images or opens a lightbox.

implementation.notes: Overlay icon (Eye or Play from lucide-react) positioned absolute on card, opacity-0 by default, opacity-100 on hover. On click: cycle through array of images within the same card frame, or open a modal/lightbox. Image transition via AnimatePresence with crossfade.

interactions.name: Click-to-Expand Half-Screen Detail View
interactions.description: Clicking a grid item (neighborhood, property, service) expands it to fill half the screen with a detailed 'flyer' view. No page navigation needed — the detail panel slides in from the right. User called the Brickell detail view 'almost sexy.'

implementation.notes: Grid of items. On click: AnimatePresence panel slides in from right (initial={{ x: '100%' }} animate={{ x: 0 }}) covering 50% of viewport width. Panel contains: hero image, title, description, stats, sub-items, CTA. Clicking outside or X button dismisses. On mobile: panel takes full width. The panel should feel like a self-contained mini-page.

layout_patterns.name: Editorial Asymmetric Grid
layout_patterns.description: Content arranged in an asymmetric CSS Grid — different block sizes, intentional whitespace, magazine-like layout. Not everything has to be the same size.

implementation.notes: CSS Grid with grid-template-columns: repeat(12, 1fr). Span different numbers of columns per element. Let some cells be empty for whitespace.

layout_patterns.name: Swiss/International Grid System
layout_patterns.description: Strict modular grid with consistent gutters. Everything aligns. Typography follows a mathematical scale. Clean, precise, systematic.

layout_patterns.name: Alternating Full-Bleed and Constrained Sections
layout_patterns.description: Some sections span the full viewport width (full-bleed images, colored backgrounds), while others are constrained to a max-width container. Creates visual rhythm and variety.

implementation.notes: Full-bleed: w-full. Constrained: max-w-7xl mx-auto px-4. Alternate between them to create rhythm.

layout_patterns.name: Single Column Editorial Reading
layout_patterns.description: Content in a narrow single column, centered. Like reading a magazine article or blog post. Maximum readability.

implementation.notes: max-w-prose sets ~65 characters per line — optimal for readability.

layout_patterns.name: Split Hero: Text Left, Image Right
layout_patterns.description: Hero section split roughly 60/40 or 50/50 — text content on the left, image or visual on the right. Clean and conversion-friendly.
